video.title: Start This Business With No Experience

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Alex Kirby, a former pastor and landscaping founder who sold his marketing agency and launched Bridgeway Global Staffing, which places vetted Latin American remote workers with US blue-collar small businesses. He claims about $100k in sales in the first 100 days from roughly 27-30 placements, charging a one-time fee of about 28% of first-year salary (roughly $4,500-5,200) plus an optional $200/month membership. The playbook covers getting first clients via texts to friends and network, sourcing and vetting talent through job boards and video applications, and a lean stack of QuickBooks plus a Lovable-built portal. Key takeaway: AI makes building easy, but distribution and proactive outreach remain the hard part.

speakers.name: Chris Koerner
speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; has hired global talent for about 15 years

speakers.name: Alex Kirby
speakers.description: Founder of Bridgeway Global Staffing; former pastor, landscaping owner and marketing agency owner

ideas.name: Bridgeway Global Staffing (overseas talent placement for blue-collar businesses)
ideas.one_liner: Recruit vetted Latin American remote workers and place them with US blue-collar small businesses for a one-time placement fee plus optional membership.
ideas.business_model: One-time placement fee (about 28% of the worker's first-year salary) plus recurring $200/month membership; employer pays the worker directly via a payroll platform.
ideas.customer: US blue-collar small business owners (landscaping, fertilization, plumbers, electricians, land clearing), mostly first-time global hirers who are overworked and need admin, marketing or customer support help.
ideas.problem: Owners work 70-hour weeks, miss calls and do invoicing at night; local admin and support hires are expensive, unreliable or hard to find; owners are unfamiliar with hiring overseas.
ideas.offer: Find, vet and introduce about four strong candidates with video intros, help interview, run a roughly 1.5 hour onboarding with a recommended tech stack, and offer a replacement guarantee (a few months without membership, six months with). Optional membership gives support, two trainings a month, a resource library and 14% fees on later hires.

pricing.model: One-time placement fee plus monthly membership

price_points.unit: of first-year salary for later hires (members)
price_points.label: Member repeat-hire fee

pricing.notes: Half paid up front and half at signing; early clients got discounts (one hire at half price) as proof of concept. Worker salaries cited around $1,200-1,600/month.

acquisition_channels.details: Texted business-owner friends and contacts met via Instagram, X and Facebook, and posted videos announcing the service and showing his own overseas team.

quote.text: I texted all my business owner friends, hey, in my town, I texted all the people I met on Instagram and X and Facebook
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

acquisition_channels.details: Uses church (about 1,200 people) and local community as the first network; advises using any nucleus such as a church, Little League or club.
Advises walking in and asking for meetings with local owners (e.g. HVAC) to pitch a beta offer.

ideas.delivery: Talent sourcing via LinkedIn ads, Facebook/Meta ads, job boards and sites like Upwork, focusing on Latin America. Candidates submit a two-minute video; Alex interviews and vets (English, degree, AI/marketing curiosity). Four candidates are shared via a Lovable-built portal; the client picks two to interview. Onboarding call about 1.5 hours, payment through Thera (or Deel/Gusto) monthly, and two membership training calls a month.
unit_economics_claims: About $100k sales in the first 100 days from roughly 26-27 clients and about 30 placements
75% of clients take the $200/month membership, roughly $4-5k/month recurring
ideas.startup_cost: About $200 / about $100 per month tech stack (QuickBooks, Wi-Fi, computer)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Built system in about 3 days; launched March 1 with a 90-day plan; $100k in first 100 days

acquisition.how: Paid ads and content can be automated, but the actual first-client route is personal texts and network outreach, which is relationship-driven and PECR-restricted for sole traders in the UK.

onboarding.how: A Lovable-built portal for applications and client intros can be mostly automated; onboarding calls and tech-stack advice need some human time or a recorded/agent-led version.

delivery.how: Vetting overseas candidates by video, interviewing, judging confidence and fit and matching to clients is human judgement; AI can screen and shortlist but placement quality depends on a human.

billing.how: QuickBooks or Stripe invoices with half-down deposits are easily automated.

support.how: Membership support, training webinars and resource library can be mostly recorded and agent-handled, with human-led calls twice a month and replacement handling.

uk_applicability.notes: Model works in principle with UK SMEs and overseas VAs, but needs changes: UK trades are the target, agency recruitment and worker-classification rules (IR35, employment status, right to work not an issue for overseas contractors but contract and tax compliance needed), GBP pricing, and US-specific '28% of salary' benchmarks. Cold outreach to sole traders by text or DM is restricted under PECR.

risks: Bad hires require replacement under the guarantee (one replaced after four days)
Concentration on niche and referral-led growth may not scale
AI may reduce demand for admin and support roles
Misclassification and payroll or tax compliance if the agency drifts into employer-of-record territory
Reputational pushback on outsourcing jobs overseas
Claims are self-reported and early (about 100 days)

tactics.name: Three-sentence text to network for first customers
steps: List business-owner friends, family, church or club contacts
Send a short three-sentence text explaining the new service
Ask for a meeting or call, or to be a first customer
Swap the industry as needed and learn each owner's needs
Take a deposit (even $100) as proof of concept

quote.text: You have to be willing to put ourselves out there either on Instagram or through text, through call
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

tactics.name: Place before you scale: take a deposit, then source talent
steps: Get a client willing to pay a deposit (half down, half at signing)
Use the commitment to justify sourcing
Do the first calls yourself to learn what a good employee looks like
Present four vetted candidates, let the client choose two to interview

quote.text: we try to find four that we think are great.
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

tactics.name: Candidate screening via video and key interview questions
steps: Require a two-minute video or audio intro before applying
Favour strong English, a degree, and AI or marketing curiosity/certifications
Ask 'Why should I hire you over somebody else?' to test confidence
Ask candidates to explain what they are great at and how they'd help the company

quote.text: we don't even let people apply if they don't send the two minute video.
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

tactics.name: Membership upsell and discounted repeat hires
steps: Offer a $200/month membership with support, two trainings a month and resources
Reduce later hire fee to 14% for members
Offer longer replacement guarantee (six months) to members

quote.text: every hire after your first one is 14%.
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

tactics.name: Pay overseas staff monthly to cut fees
steps: Use Thera, Deel or Gusto for compliant payments
Encourage clients to pay once a month so transfer fees are incurred once

quote.text: we like to do it once a month. That way the fees are only one time.
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

tactics.name: Show up in person when emails go unanswered
steps: Pick a warm prospect who has replied at least once
Dress professionally and arrive as if expected
Ask for the decision-maker and remove friction by solving their problem in person

quote.text: I faked a meeting, I dressed up, I put my laptop in briefcase
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

tactics.name: Niche down to a vertical you know
steps: Choose a segment where you speak the language (blue collar)
Lean in publicly and accept losing off-niche leads

quote.text: I think it's smart to be focused first and then if it demand grows, then you can figure that out later.
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

warnings.warning: AI has made building easier but not business easier; distribution and getting customers is harder because everyone can build the same thing.

quote.text: I don't think AI has made business any easier. It just makes it simpler.
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

warnings.warning: Waiting for customers does not work; most people skip the hard outreach step.

quote.text: I'm waiting for customers. And I'm like, that's like fishing without bait, man.
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

warnings.warning: Customers don't think about you; expect to follow up many times.

quote.text: You have to send 13 reminder emails. They don't care about you at all.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Timing risk: launching a content agency just as ChatGPT arrived gutted revenue.
Impressive CVs don't guarantee fit; one Microsoft-experienced hire was replaced after four days for poor personality fit for customer support.
A broad staffing offer could dilute positioning; an advisor warned him to lean into blue collar rather than also serving insurance.

lessons.lesson: Building software with AI tools now takes days; the scarce skill is distribution and willingness to reach out personally.

quote.text: which of those 13 guys is gonna be willing to text the 60 friends and family?
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

lessons.lesson: Start with your existing network and unfair advantage (church, club, community) to get first customers and a deposit.

quote.text: Everyone has an unfair advantage.
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

lessons.lesson: A favour you already do for free (connecting people with jobs) can be a monetisable business; check what others pay for the same service.
Place-and-leave recruiting is lower-headache than a staffing agency that carries payroll and compliance, at the cost of lower lifetime revenue; a membership adds recurring income.
Specialise in a vertical you understand deeply so you can speak the language with confidence.
Early discounts and deposits are a cheap way to get proof of concept and testimonials.
Most clients (about 90%) hire to add capacity as the business grows, not to replace local staff, which helps position the offer.
Humans plus AI is positioned as more durable than pure AI replacement for support roles; remote talent plus AI tools is the value proposition.

quote.text: I think global talent plus AI is the absolute sauce, the game changer.
quote.speaker: Alex Kirby

lessons.lesson: Add or remove friction deliberately in habits and sales; removing the buyer's friction (showing up in person) closed a big contract.
Use business to buy back time for family rather than as an end in itself.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific figures (28% fee, $4.5-5.2k ticket, 75% membership take rate, ~30 placements), but results cover only about 100 days, are self-reported and unverified, and the Whisper-tiny transcript garbles some details.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host sells a $19 business plan and TKO Owners community and a paid YouTube membership; guest promotes Bridgeway Global Staffing.
